title.zh: 卷五十九 列傳第十九 殷淳 張暢 何偃 江智淵
title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 19: Yin Chun, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan
title.raw: 卷五十九 列傳第十九 殷淳 張暢 何偃 江智淵 Volume 59 Biographies 19: Yin Chun, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan

sentences.zh: 列傳第十九 殷淳子孚弟沖淡張暢何偃江智淵

translations.literal: Biography 19: Yin Chun, his son Fu, younger brothers Chong and Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, Jiang Zhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Biography 19: Yin Chun, Yin Fu, Yin Chong, Yin Dan, Zhang Chang, He Yan, and Jiang Zhiyuan

sentences.zh: 淳少好學，有美名。

translations.literal: Chun from youth loved learning and had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chun was studious from childhood and enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平初，為秘書郎，衡陽王文學，秘書丞，中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingping under the Young Emperor, he served as Secretariat Gentleman, Literary Scholar for the Prince of Hengyang, Secretariat Assistant, and Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingping era under Emperor Shao, he held the posts of Secretariat Gentleman, literary attendant to the Prince of Hengyang, Secretariat aide, and Secretariat Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 淳居黃門為清切，下直應留下省，以父老特聽還家。

translations.literal: Chun's position in the Yellow Gate was pure and exacting; after duty he ought to remain at the Secretariat, but because his father was aged he was specially permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chun's palace posting was demanding; after his shift he was normally required to stay at the Secretariat compound, but because his father was elderly he received special permission to go home.

sentences.zh: 高簡寡欲，早有清尚，愛好文義，未嘗違舍。

translations.literal: He was lofty and spare, with few desires; early he had pure aspirations; he loved literary principles and never neglected them.
translations.idiomatic: Aloof and abstemious, he had cultivated refined tastes from early on and pursued literary and scholarly interests without ever setting them aside.

sentences.zh: 在秘書閣撰《四部書目》凡四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat Pavilion he compiled the Catalogue of the Four Divisions in forty juan total, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Secretariat archives he compiled the forty-juan Catalogue of Works in Four Categories, which was published and widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十一年卒，時年三十二，朝廷痛惜之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanjia he died, aged thirty-two; the court deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Yuanjia (434), at the age of thirty-two; the court grieved deeply for his loss.

sentences.zh: 子孚，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Fu had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Fu inherited his father's character.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明末，為始興相。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, he served as Chancellor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Daming era under Emperor Xiaowu, he served as prefect of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 官至尚書吏部郎，順帝撫軍長史。

translations.literal: His office reached Ministerial Recorder in the Ministry of Personnel; Chief Secretary to the Pacification Army under Emperor Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and served as chief secretary on the crown prince's staff under Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 淳弟沖，字希遠，歷中書黃門郎，坐議事不當免。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Chong, style Xiyuan, passed through Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat; he was dismissed for improper counsel in deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chun's younger brother Yin Chong, styled Xiyuan, served as a Central Secretariat palace attendant but was dismissed when his advice at council proved unsound.

sentences.zh: 復為太子中庶子，尚書吏部郎，御史中丞，有司直之稱。

translations.literal: He was again made Crown Prince Household Companion, Ministerial Recorder, and Imperial Censor; he had the reputation of a straight officer of government.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as a household companion to the crown prince, then Director of Personnel and Imperial Censor, earning a reputation as an upright and uncompromising official.

sentences.zh: 出為吳興太守，入為度支尚書。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Wuxing and entered as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as governor of Wuxing and recalled to serve as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元兇妃即淳女，而沖在東宮為劭所知遇；

translations.literal: The consort of the Depraved One was Chun's daughter, and Chong in the Eastern Palace was known and favored by Shao;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Liu Shao's consort was Yin Chun's daughter, and Yin Chong won favor with Shao while serving in the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 劭弑立，以為侍中、護軍，遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: when Shao assassinated and established himself, he made him Palace Attendant and Protector of the Army, then transferred him to Director of the Metropolitan Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: after Shao seized the throne by murdering his father, he appointed Chong Palace Attendant and Protector-General of the Army, then promoted him to metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 沖有學義文辭，劭使為尚書符，罪狀世祖，亦為劭盡力。

translations.literal: Chong had learning, principles, and literary skill; Shao made him draft the Secretariat dispatch indicting Emperor Xiaowu, and he also exerted himself fully for Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong was learned and a skilled writer; Shao had him draft the formal indictment of Emperor Xiaowu for the Secretariat records, and Chong served Shao's cause with all his ability.

sentences.zh: 世祖克京邑，賜死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the capital, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu recaptured the capital, Chong was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 沖弟淡，字夷遠，亦歷黃門吏部郎，太子中庶子，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Dan, style Yiyuan, also passed through Yellow Gate and Ministerial Recorder posts, Crown Prince Household Companion, and Colonel in charge of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong's younger brother Yin Dan, styled Yiyuan, likewise held posts as palace attendant and director in the Ministry of Personnel, crown prince's household companion, and commanding colonel of the footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 大明世，以文章見知，為當時才士。

translations.literal: In the Daming era he was known for his writings and was a talented man of the time.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming reign he gained recognition for his literary work and was counted among the leading writers of the age.

sentences.zh: 張暢，字少微，吳郡吳人，吳興太守邵兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang, style Shaowei, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery, nephew of Wuxing Governor Shao by his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang, styled Shaowei, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery and the nephew of Shao, governor of Wuxing, on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 父禕，少有孝行，歷宦州府，為琅邪王國郎中令。

translations.literal: His father Yi in youth had filial conduct; he passed through offices in prefectures and provinces and served as Administrator of Gentlemen in the Kingdom of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yi was known for filial devotion from youth and served in regional government until he was appointed chief of gentlemen in the principality of Langye.

sentences.zh: 從琅邪王至洛。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Prince of Langye to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 還京都，高祖封藥酒一罌付禕，使密加鴆毒。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Emperor Gaozu sealed a jar of medicinal wine and entrusted it to Yi, ordering him secretly to add hemlock poison.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey to the capital, Emperor Gaozu gave Yi a sealed jar of medicinal wine with orders to lace it secretly with lethal poison.

sentences.zh: 禕受命，既還，於道自飲而卒。

translations.literal: Yi received the command; once returned, on the road he drank it himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi accepted the charge, and on the way home he drank the wine himself and died.

sentences.zh: 暢少與從兄敷、演、敬齊名，為後進之秀。

translations.literal: Chang in youth with his older cousins Fu, Yan, and Jing was equally famous, an outstanding figure among the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang in his youth was ranked with his cousins Zhang Fu, Zhang Yan, and Zhang Jing among the most promising younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 起家為太守徐佩之主簿，佩之被誅，暢馳出奔赴，制服盡哀，為論者所美。

translations.literal: At his first emergence he was Registrar to Governor Xu Peizhi; when Peizhi was executed, Chang galloped out to rush to him, donned mourning garb with full grief, and was praised by commentators.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as chief clerk to Governor Xu Peizhi; when Xu was executed, Chang raced to the scene, put on mourning dress, and grieved wholeheartedly — conduct that critics praised.

sentences.zh: 弟牧嘗為猘犬所傷，醫云宜食蝦蟆膾，牧甚難之，暢含笑先嘗，牧因此乃食，創亦即愈。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mu had once been wounded by a mad dog; the doctor said he should eat minced toad; Mu found it very difficult; Chang with a smile tasted it first, and Mu therefore ate, and the wound then quickly healed.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Zhang Mu was bitten by a rabid dog, the physician prescribed minced toad; Mu recoiled at the idea, but Chang smilingly tasted it first, whereupon Mu ate as well and the wound soon healed.

sentences.zh: 州辟從事，衡陽王義季征虜行參軍，彭城王義康平北主簿，司徒祭酒，尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Aide; Staff Officer on the campaign staff of the Prince of Hengyang Yiji; Chief Clerk for the northern campaign of the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; Libationer of the Minister of Education; Master of Guests in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial authorities appointed him as an aide; he served as campaign staff officer to Prince Yiji of Hengyang and chief clerk on Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's northern staff, then as libationer to the Ministry of Education and master of foreign receptions at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未拜，又除度支左民郎，江夏王義恭征北記室參軍、晉安太守。

translations.literal: Before he had accepted appointment, he was again given Left Bureau Officer of Revenue and Army Staff Recorder on the northern expedition of the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, and Governor of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up one of these posts, he was appointed revenue officer in the left bureau, staff secretary on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's northern command, and governor of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 又為義季安西記室參軍、南義陽太守，臨川王義慶衛軍從事中郎，揚州治中別駕從事史，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He again served as Army Staff Recorder for Yiji's Anxi command, Governor of Southern Yiyang, Attendant on the Military Staff of the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, Director of the Secretariat of Yang Province, and Crown Prince Household Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff secretary on Prince Yiji's western command and as governor of southern Yiyang, then as attendant on Prince Yiqing of Linchuan's military staff, Yangzhou secretariat director, and crown prince's household companion.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮彭城，暢為安北長史、沛郡太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu held Pengcheng, Chang was Chief Secretary for the Pacification of the North and Governor of Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Xiaowu was stationed at Pengcheng, Zhang Chang served as his chief secretary and as governor of Pei.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，索虜托跋燾南侵，太尉江夏王義恭揔統諸軍，出鎮彭、泗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Northern Barbarians under Tuoba Tao invaded south; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia commanded all armies and went out to hold Peng and Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia (450), the Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao invaded the south; Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia took overall command of the armies and moved to defend Peng and Si.

sentences.zh: 時燾親率大眾，已至蕭城，去彭城十數里。

translations.literal: At that time Tao personally led a great host and had already reached Xiaocheng, a dozen li from Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tao himself was leading a massive army and had already reached Xiaocheng, only some ten-odd li from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彭城眾力雖多，而軍食不足，義恭欲棄彭城南歸，計議彌日不定。

translations.literal: Though Pengcheng's forces were numerous, military grain was insufficient; Yigong wished to abandon Pengcheng and return south; deliberation went on for days without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng had ample troops but meager supplies; Yigong wanted to abandon the city and retreat south, yet the council debated for days without reaching a decision.

sentences.zh: 時歷城眾少食多，安北中兵參軍沈慶之建議，欲以車營為函箱陣，精兵為外翼。

translations.literal: At that time Licheng had few people but much grain; Army Staff Officer Shen Qingzhi of the Pacification of the North proposed using the wagon camp in a box-formation, elite troops as outer wings.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng had a small garrison but abundant grain; Shen Qingzhi, army staff officer on the northern command, proposed forming wagons into a boxed formation with picked troops as an outer shield,

sentences.zh: 奉二王及妃媛直趨歷城；

translations.literal: escorting the two princes and their consorts straight to Licheng;
translations.idiomatic: escorting the two princes and their consorts directly to Licheng,

sentences.zh: 分兵配護軍蕭思話留守。

translations.literal: dividing troops assigned to Protector of the Army Xiao Sihua to remain and hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: while detaching troops for Protector-General Xiao Sihua to hold Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史何勖不同，欲席捲奔鬱洲，自海道還京都。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Chief Secretary He Xu dissented, wishing to roll up and flee to Yuzhou, returning to the capital by the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal's chief secretary He Xu disagreed, preferring a swift withdrawal to Yuzhou and a sea voyage back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 義恭去意已判，唯二議未決，更集群僚謀之。

translations.literal: Yigong's intent to leave was already settled, but only these two plans were undecided, so he again gathered the assembled officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's mind was set on withdrawal, but with two routes still in dispute, he summoned the staff once more for counsel.

sentences.zh: 眾咸惶擾，莫有異議。

translations.literal: The multitude were all fearful and agitated; none had a dissenting view.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was gripped by panic, and no one voiced opposition to flight.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「若歷城、鬱洲有可致之理，下官敢不高贊。

translations.literal: Chang said: "If Licheng and Yuzhou were attainable in principle, your subordinate would not dare fail to lend high support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang said, "If Licheng or Yuzhou were genuinely within reach, I would not hesitate to endorse the plan wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 今城內乏食，百姓咸有走情，但以關扃嚴固，欲去莫從耳。

translations.literal: Now within the city food is scarce; common folk all have fleeing hearts, but only because the barriers are strictly closed they wish to leave and cannot.
translations.idiomatic: The city is short of food, and the people are desperate to flee — but the gates are locked tight, so they cannot scatter even if they wish to.

sentences.zh: 若一旦動腳，則各自散走，欲至所在，何由可得。

translations.literal: If once feet are set in motion, then each will scatter on his own; wishing to reach the intended place, how could one obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Once the army stirs, everyone will break and run in every direction — who could then expect to arrive anywhere together?

sentences.zh: 今軍食雖寡，朝夕猶未窘罄，量其欲盡，臨時更為諸宜，豈有舍萬安之術，而就危亡之道。

translations.literal: Now though military grain is scant, morning and evening it is not yet utterly exhausted; estimating when it will run out, at the time one can make further arrangements — how could there be abandoning a ten-thousand-fold safe plan and taking the road of peril and ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Our rations are thin, but we are not yet at the brink from day to day; when supplies do run low, we can adjust then. Why abandon a sound position for a gamble on disaster?

sentences.zh: 若此計必用，下官請以頸血汙公馬蹄！」

translations.literal: If this plan must be used, your subordinate asks to stain the Duke's horse's hoofs with the blood of his neck!"
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on this course, I ask leave to stain your horse's hoofs with my blood!"

sentences.zh: 世祖既聞暢議，謂義恭曰：「阿父既為揔統，去留非所敢干。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu having heard Chang's discussion, said to Yigong: "Uncle, as you command in chief, going or staying is not what I dare meddle in.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Zhang Chang's argument, the future Emperor Xiaowu told Yigong, "Father, you command the army — whether we stay or go is not for me to decide.

sentences.zh: 道民忝為城主，而損威延寇，其為愧恧，亦已深矣。

translations.literal: Daomin humbly serves as lord of the city, yet in diminishing prestige and prolonging the enemy, the shame I feel is already deep.
translations.idiomatic: As lord of this city I have already shamed us by letting the enemy advance — my guilt runs deep enough.

sentences.zh: 委鎮奔逃，實無顏復奉朝廷，期與此城共其存沒，張長史言不可異也。」

translations.literal: To abandon the fortress and flee — truly I have no face to serve the court again; I expect to share survival and destruction with this city; Chief Secretary Zhang's words may not differ."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon Pengcheng would leave me no honor to face the court again. I mean to live or die with this fortress, and I cannot dissent from Chief Secretary Zhang."

sentences.zh: 暢言既堅，世祖又贊成其議，義恭乃止。

translations.literal: Chang's words being firm, and Emperor Xiaowu also supporting his view, Yigong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang held firm, the prince backed him, and Yigong abandoned the retreat.

sentences.zh: 時太祖遣員外散騎侍郎徐爰乘驛至彭城取米穀定最，爰既去，城內遣騎送之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizu sent Supernumerary Cavalry Attendant Xu Ai by post relay to Pengcheng to secure the grain reckoning; after Ai had departed, within the city they sent riders to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had dispatched Xu Ai on the courier route to audit Pengcheng's grain stores; after he left, the garrison sent escorts after him.

sentences.zh: 燾聞知，即遣數百騎急追，爰已過淮，僅得免。

translations.literal: Tao heard and at once sent several hundred riders in urgent pursuit; Ai had already crossed the Huai and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tao learned of this and immediately sent several hundred horsemen in hot pursuit; Xu had already crossed the Huai and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 初爰去，城內聞虜遣追，慮爰見禽，失米最，慮知城內食少，義恭憂懼無計，猶欲奔走。

translations.literal: At first when Ai departed, within the city they heard the barbarians sent pursuit, feared Ai would be captured and the grain reckoning lost, feared they would learn food within was scant; Yigong worried without plan and still wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu left, word spread that the Wei were pursuing him; fearing his capture would reveal both the audit and the city's hunger, Yigong again panicked and nearly fled.

sentences.zh: 爰既免，其日虜大眾亦至彭城。

translations.literal: Ai having escaped, that same day the barbarians' great host also reached Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu escaped that day — and the main Northern Wei army reached Pengcheng the same day.

sentences.zh: 燾始至，仍登城南亞父塚，於戲馬台立氈屋。

translations.literal: Tao having first arrived, forthwith ascended Yafu's mound south of the city and erected a felt tent on the Horse-Playing Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Tao arrived and at once climbed Yafu's mound south of the city, where he pitched a felt pavilion on the Horse-Playing Terrace.

sentences.zh: 先是，燾未至，世祖遣將馬文恭向蕭城，為虜所破，文恭走得免，隊主蒯應見執。

translations.literal: Before this, before Tao arrived, Emperor Xiaowu sent the officer Ma Wengong toward Xiaocheng; he was defeated by the barbarians; Wengong ran and escaped; squad leader Kuai Ying was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Tao arrived, the prince had sent Ma Wengong toward Xiaocheng; the Wei routed him — Ma fled, but squad leader Kuai Ying was captured.

sentences.zh: 至小市門曰：「魏主致意安北，遠來疲乏，若有甘蔗及酒，可見分。」

translations.literal: At the Small Market Gate he said: "The Wei ruler sends greetings to the Pacification of the North; coming from afar we are weary — if there is sugarcane and wine, you might share some."
translations.idiomatic: At the Small Market Gate he said, "The Wei ruler sends his regards to the Pacifier of the North: we are weary from the long march — if you have sugarcane and wine, might we have a share?

sentences.zh: 時防城隊主梁法念答曰：「當為啟聞。」

translations.literal: The city-defense squad leader Liang Fanian answered: "I shall report this upward."
translations.idiomatic: The garrison squad leader Liang Fanian replied, "I shall report this to my superiors.

sentences.zh: 應乃自陳蕭城之敗。

translations.literal: Ying then on his own stated the defeat at Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai then volunteered an account of the defeat at Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 又問應：「虜主自來不？」

translations.literal: They again asked Ying: "Has the barbarian ruler come in person?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked Kuai further, "Has the Wei ruler come in person?

translations.literal: He said: "He has come."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He has.

sentences.zh: 問：「今何在？」

translations.literal: They asked: "Where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 應舉手指西南。

translations.literal: Ying raised his hand and pointed southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai raised his hand and pointed southwest.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「士馬多少？」

translations.literal: They again said: "How many men and horses?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "How many men and horses?

sentences.zh: 答云：「四十餘萬。」

translations.literal: He answered: "More than four hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "More than four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 法念以燾語白世祖，世祖遣人答曰：「知行路多乏，今付酒二器，甘蔗百挺。

translations.literal: Fanian reported Tao's words to Emperor Xiaowu; Emperor Xiaowu sent someone to answer: "Knowing the road has been much exhausting, we now deliver two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.
translations.idiomatic: Fanian reported Tao's message to the prince, who sent a reply: "Knowing how taxing the march has been, we send two jars of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 聞彼有駱駝，可遣送。」

translations.literal: We hear you have camels — you may send them over."
translations.idiomatic: We hear you have camels — kindly send some over."

sentences.zh: 明旦，燾又自上戲馬台，復遣使至小市門曰：「魏主致意安北，安北可暫出門，欲與安北相見。

translations.literal: Next dawn Tao again ascended the Horse-Playing Terrace and again sent an envoy to the Small Market Gate saying: "The Wei ruler sends greetings to the Pacification of the North; the Pacification of the North may briefly come out the gate — he wishes to meet the Pacification of the North.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Tao again mounted the Horse-Playing Terrace and sent another envoy to the Small Market Gate: "The Wei ruler greets the Pacifier of the North and asks that he step briefly outside the gate for a meeting.

sentences.zh: 我亦不攻此城，安北何勞苦將士在城上。

translations.literal: I also will not attack this city — why should the Pacification of the North trouble his officers and soldiers on the walls?
translations.idiomatic: I do not mean to assault this city — why should the Pacifier of the North weary his men on the ramparts?

sentences.zh: 又騾、驢、駱駝，是北國所出，今遣送，並致雜物。」

translations.literal: Again, mules, donkeys, and camels are products of the northern state — we now send them and also present miscellaneous goods."
translations.idiomatic: Mules, donkeys, and camels are native to our north — we now send them, along with other gifts.

sentences.zh: 又語小市門隊主曰：「既有餉物，君可移度南門受之。」

translations.literal: He also told the Small Market Gate squad leader: "Since there are presented goods, you may shift to the South Gate to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the squad leader at the Small Market Gate, "Since gifts are coming, you may move to the South Gate to receive them.

sentences.zh: 燾送駱駝、騾、馬及貂裘、雜飲食，既至南門，門先閉，請龠未出。

translations.literal: Tao sent camels, mules, horses, sable furs, and miscellaneous food and drink; when they reached the South Gate, the gate was already closed and the request for the gate-bar had not yet come out.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent camels, mules, horses, sable furs, and assorted food and drink; when they reached the South Gate it was already shut, and the order to open it had not yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 暢於城上視之，虜使問：「是張長史邪？」

translations.literal: Chang watched from atop the wall; the barbarian envoy asked: "Is that Chief Secretary Zhang?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang watched from the wall; the Wei envoy asked, "Is that Chief Secretary Zhang?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「君何得見識？」

translations.literal: Chang said: "How do you recognize me?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "How do you know who I am?

sentences.zh: 虜使答云：「君聲名遠聞，足使我知。」

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy answered: "Your fame is heard from afar — enough to let me know."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, "Your reputation travels far — that is enough for me to know.

sentences.zh: 暢因問虜使姓，答云：「我是鮮卑，無姓。

translations.literal: Chang then asked the barbarian envoy's surname; he answered: "I am Xianbei — I have no surname.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then asked the envoy's surname; he answered, "I am Xianbei — we have no surnames.

sentences.zh: 且道亦不可。」

translations.literal: And the Way also may not be spoken."
translations.idiomatic: And I may not speak of the Way either.

sentences.zh: 暢又問：「君居何任？」

translations.literal: Chang again asked: "What office do you hold?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang asked again, "What is your office?

sentences.zh: 答云：「鮮卑官位不同，不可輒道，然亦足與君相敵耳。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Xianbei offices differ — I may not speak of them lightly, yet they are enough to match you."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Xianbei ranks do not correspond to yours, so I cannot name mine readily — but they are sufficient to match yours.

sentences.zh: 虜使復問：「何為匆匆杜門絕橋？」

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy again asked: "Why have you hastily barred the gates and cut the bridges?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy asked again, "Why have you so hastily shut the gates and cut the bridges?

sentences.zh: 暢答曰：「二王以魏主營壘未立，將士疲勞，此精甲十萬，人思致命，恐輕相淩踐，故且閉城耳。

translations.literal: Chang answered: "The two princes, because the Wei ruler's camp and ramparts are not yet established and the officers and soldiers are weary — here are a hundred thousand in elite armor, each man thinking to give his life — fear a light mutual trampling, so for now the city is closed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang answered, "The two princes note that the Wei ruler's camp is not yet set and your troops are weary. We have a hundred thousand men in fine armor, each ready to die — we feared a rash clash, so the gates stay closed for now.

sentences.zh: 待彼休息士馬，然後共治戰場，克日交戲。」

translations.literal: Wait until their men and horses rest, then together fix the battlefield and set a day for contest."
translations.idiomatic: When your men and horses have rested, we shall fix the field and set a day for battle.

sentences.zh: 虜使曰：「君當以法令裁物，何用發橋，復何足以十萬誇人。

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy said: "You ought to measure things by law and ordinance — what use is raising bridges? And what makes a hundred thousand enough to boast to others?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "You should govern by law — why raise bridges? And what makes a mere hundred thousand worth boasting about?

sentences.zh: 我亦有良馬逸足，若雲騎四集，亦可以相拒。」

translations.literal: I too have fine horses with swift feet — if cloud-riders gather on four sides, they also can resist."
translations.idiomatic: We too have fine horses and swift mounts — if horsemen gather from every quarter, they can hold their own.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「侯王設嶮，何但法令而已邪？

translations.literal: Chang said: "When feudal lords set defenses, is it only by law and ordinance?
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "When princes fortify a place, do they rely on law alone?

sentences.zh: 我若誇君，當言百萬。

translations.literal: If I were to boast to you, I should say a million.
translations.idiomatic: If I wished to boast to you, I would say a million.

sentences.zh: 所以言十萬者，政二王左右素所畜養者耳。

translations.literal: The reason I speak of a hundred thousand is simply the men the two princes have long kept and nurtured at their sides.
translations.idiomatic: I said a hundred thousand only because that is the force the two princes have long kept at their side.

sentences.zh: 此城內有數州士庶，二徒營伍，猶所未論。

translations.literal: Within this city are commoners and gentry from several provinces, and two groups of camp soldiers — these are still not reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: The civilians of several provinces within these walls, and the two divisions of camp troops, I have not even counted.

sentences.zh: 我本鬥智，不鬥馬足。

translations.literal: I by nature contend in wits, not in horses' feet.
translations.idiomatic: I contend in wits, not in horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 且冀之北土，馬之所生，君復何以逸足見誇邪！」

translations.literal: Moreover, north of Ji is the land where horses are born — with what swift feet would you again boast to me!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the lands north of Ji are where horses are bred — with what swift mounts do you boast to me!

sentences.zh: 虜使曰：「不爾。

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 城守，君之所長；

translations.literal: Holding a city — that is your strength;
translations.idiomatic: Holding cities is your strength;

sentences.zh: 野戰，我之所長。

translations.literal: field battle — that is my strength.
translations.idiomatic: field battle is mine.

sentences.zh: 我之恃馬，猶如君之恃城耳。」

translations.literal: My relying on horses is just like your relying on the city.
translations.idiomatic: My reliance on horses is like your reliance on walls.

sentences.zh: 城內有具思者，嘗在北國，義恭遣視之，思識是虜尚書李孝伯。

translations.literal: Within the city was Ju Si, who had once been in the northern state; Yigong sent him to look — Si recognized him as the barbarian Minister Li Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city was Ju Si, who had once served in the north; Yigong sent him to look and Si recognized the Wei minister Li Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 思因問：「李尚書，若行途有勞。」

translations.literal: Si then asked: "Minister Li, you must be weary from the journey."
translations.idiomatic: Si then asked, "Minister Li, you must be weary from the road.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「此事應相與共知。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "This matter ought to be mutually known."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "That is something we should both know.

sentences.zh: 思答：「緣共知，所以有勞。」

translations.literal: Si answered: "Because we mutually know, therefore there is weariness."
translations.idiomatic: Si answered, "Because we both know it, that is why you are weary.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「感君至意。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I am moved by your utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "I am touched by your kindness."

sentences.zh: 既開門，暢屏卻人仗，出對孝伯，並進餉物。

translations.literal: Once the gate was opened, Chang dismissed armed attendants and went out to face Xiaobo, and together they advanced the presented goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the gate opened, Chang sent away armed escorts and went out to meet Xiaobo, and they brought in the gifts together.

sentences.zh: 虜使云：「貂裘與太尉，駱駝、騾與安北，蒲陶酒雜飲，叔侄共嘗。」

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy said: "The sable fur is for the Grand Marshal, camels and mules for the Pacification of the North, grape wine and miscellaneous drink — uncle and nephew shall taste together."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "The sable coat is for the Grand Marshal, the camels and mules for the Pacifier of the North, and the grape wine and assorted drinks are for uncle and nephew to share."

sentences.zh: 燾又乞酒並甘橘。

translations.literal: Tao again requested wine and sweet oranges.
translations.idiomatic: Tao also asked for wine and sweet oranges.

sentences.zh: 暢宣世祖問：「致意魏主，知欲相見，常遲面寫。

translations.literal: Chang conveyed Emperor Xiaowu's inquiry: "Convey my regards to the Wei ruler — knowing he wishes to meet, I have long awaited a face-to-face audience.
translations.idiomatic: Chang relayed Emperor Xiaowu's message: "Please tell the Wei ruler that, knowing he wishes to meet, I have long looked forward to a face-to-face audience.

sentences.zh: 但受命本朝，過蒙藩任，人臣無境外之交，恨不暫悉。

translations.literal: But having received commission from this court and having been excessively entrusted with a border post, a minister has no dealings beyond the state — I regret we cannot even briefly know each other fully.
translations.idiomatic: But I hold my commission from this court and have been entrusted with a frontier post beyond my merits; a subject may not maintain ties across the border — I regret we cannot meet even briefly.

sentences.zh: 且城守備防，邊鎮之常，但悅以使之，故勞而無怨耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, holding a city and standing on guard are the constant duties of a border garrison; it is only because pleasure in the assignment makes them serve, so they toil without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, holding a city and standing on guard are the routine duties of a frontier command; it is only because our men take pride in their task that they toil without complaint.

sentences.zh: 太尉、鎮軍得所送物，魏主意，知復須甘橘，今並付如別。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and the Field Marshal have received the items sent; the Wei ruler's intent — knowing he again needs sweet oranges — now all are delivered as listed separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal and the Field Marshal have received your gifts. Learning that the Wei ruler also wants sweet oranges, we are sending them as listed separately.

sentences.zh: 太尉以北土寒鄉，皮絝褶脫是所須，今致魏主。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, because the northern land is a cold country, sends leather trousers and coats, which are what is needed — now presenting them to the Wei ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal notes that the north is a cold land and sends leather breeches and coats, which you should find useful, as a gift to the Wei ruler.

sentences.zh: 螺杯、雜粽，南土所珍，鎮軍今以相致。」

translations.literal: Spiral-shell cups and assorted rice dumplings, treasures of the southern land — the Field Marshal now sends them as gifts."
translations.idiomatic: Spiral-shell cups and assorted zongzi, delicacies of the south — the Field Marshal sends them now as gifts.

sentences.zh: 此信未去，燾復遣使令孝伯傳語曰：「魏主有詔語太尉、安北，近以騎至，車兩在後，今端坐無為，有博具可見借。」

translations.literal: Before this message had even gone out, Tao again sent an envoy to have Xiaobo relay words: "The Wei ruler has an edict for the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North: I have just arrived with cavalry, wagons following behind; sit at ease and do nothing — if you have gaming pieces, may I borrow them?"
translations.idiomatic: Before this message had even gone out, Tao sent another envoy through Xiaobo with a message: "The Wei ruler has an edict for the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North: my cavalry has just arrived and the wagons are behind; rest easy and stay put — if you have gaming pieces, lend us some.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「博具當為申啟。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The gaming pieces will be reported up for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "I shall report your request for gaming pieces.

sentences.zh: 但向語二王，已非遜辭，且有詔之言，政可施於彼國，何得稱之於此。」

translations.literal: But the words just spoken to the two princes were already not modest language, and talk of an edict properly applies only in your state — how can such language be used here?"
translations.idiomatic: But what you just said to the two princes was hardly deferential, and language of imperial edicts belongs in your realm — how can you use it here?

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「詔之與語，朕之與我，竝有何異。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Between 'edict' and 'speech,' between 'We' and 'I' — what difference is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "What difference is there between an edict and ordinary speech, or between 'We' and 'I'?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「若辭以通，可如來談；

translations.literal: Chang said: "If words were interchangeable, your argument might stand;
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "If terms were interchangeable, you might have a point;

sentences.zh: 既言有所施，則貴賤有等。

translations.literal: once it is said there is something to which a term applies, then noble and base have their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: but once you say a term applies only in certain cases, rank and station matter.

sentences.zh: 向所稱詔，非所敢聞。」

translations.literal: The 'edict' just mentioned is not what I dare hear."
translations.idiomatic: The 'edict' you just used is not something I may hear in this place.

sentences.zh: 孝伯又曰：「太尉、安北是人臣與非？」

translations.literal: Xiaobo again said: "Are the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North subjects or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo pressed on: "Are the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North not subjects?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "They are."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "They are.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「鄰國之君，何為不稱詔於鄰國之臣？」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The ruler of a neighboring state — why may he not use the word 'edict' toward ministers of a neighboring state?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Why should the ruler of a neighboring state not speak of an edict to ministers of a neighboring state?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「君之此稱，尚不可聞於中華，況在諸王之貴，而猶曰鄰國之君邪。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Your use of this term could not even be spoken in the Central Realm; how much less when addressing princes of noble rank — and you still call him merely 'ruler of a neighboring state'?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "That word would not even be permissible in the Central Realm; how much less when addressing princes of the blood — and you still say 'ruler of a neighboring state'?

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「魏主言太尉、鎮軍並皆年少，分闊南信，殊當憂邑。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The Wei ruler says the Grand Marshal and the Field Marshal are both young, separated from the south by a wide gulf, and must be deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Wei ruler observes that the Grand Marshal and the Field Marshal are both young, cut off from news of the south, and must be anxious indeed.

sentences.zh: 若欲遣信者，當為護送；

translations.literal: If you wish to send envoys, he will escort them;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to send envoys, he will see them safely through;

sentences.zh: 脫須騎者，亦當以馬送之。」

translations.literal: if you need riders, he will also provide horses to send them."
translations.idiomatic: if you need couriers, he will supply horses as well.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「此方間路甚多，使命日夕往來，不復以此勞魏主。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "There are many secret routes in this region; envoys come and go day and night — we need not burden the Wei ruler with this."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "There are many byways here, and messengers pass day and night — we need not trouble the Wei ruler for that.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「亦知有水路，似為白賊所斷。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I also know there is a water route — it seems cut off by the white bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "We know there is also a water route — but it seems blocked by the White Bandits.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「君著白衣，故稱白賊邪？」

translations.literal: Chang said: "You wear white robes — is that why you call them 'white bandits'?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "You wear white — is that why you say 'White Bandits'?

sentences.zh: 孝伯大笑曰：「今之白賊，亦不異黃巾、赤眉。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo laughed loudly and said: "Today's white bandits are no different from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo laughed and said, "Today's White Bandits are no different from the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「黃巾、赤眉，似不在江南。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "The Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows — they do not seem to have been in Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows were hardly in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「雖不在江南，亦不在青、徐也。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Though not in Jiangnan, they were also not in Qing and Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "They were not in Jiangnan — but they were not in Qing and Xu either.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「今者青、徐，實為有賊，但非白賊耳。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "As for Qing and Xu today, there truly are bandits — only they are not white bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "As for Qing and Xu today, there are indeed bandits — just not White Bandits.

sentences.zh: 虜使云：「向借博具，何故不出？」

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy said: "You were asked to lend gaming pieces — why have they not come out?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "We asked to borrow gaming pieces — why haven't they appeared?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「二王貴遠，啟聞難徹。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "The two princes are nobly distant; it is hard to get a reply through to them."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The two princes are far above us; it is hard to get their answer in time.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「周公握髮吐哺，二王何獨貴遠？」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The Duke of Zhou grasped his hair and spat out his meal — why are the two princes alone so nobly distant?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Duke of Zhou would break off his toilet to receive guests — why should the two princes alone be 'too high to reach'?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「握髮吐飡，本施中國耳。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Grasping hair and spitting out food — that practice belongs only to the Central Realm."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "That custom of breaking off a meal to receive guests belongs to the Central Realm alone.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「賓有禮，主則擇之。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "When the guest is courteous, the host may choose his response."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "When the guest observes propriety, the host may choose how to respond.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「昨見眾賓至門，未為有禮。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Yesterday I saw your many guests arrive at the gate — that was not courteous."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Yesterday I saw your horde arrive at the gate — that was hardly courteous.

sentences.zh: 俄頃送博具出，因以與之。

translations.literal: Before long gaming pieces were sent out and given to them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the gaming pieces were brought out and handed over.

sentences.zh: 燾又遣人云：「魏主致意安北，程天祚一介常人，誠知非宋朝之美，近於汝陽身被九創，落在殿外，我手牽而出之。

translations.literal: Tao again sent someone to say: "The Wei ruler sends regards to the Pacifier of the North. Cheng Tianzuo is a mere ordinary man — he truly knows he is not fine talent of the Song court. Recently at Ruyang he received nine wounds, fell outside the hall, and I pulled him out by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent another message: "The Wei ruler sends his regards to the Pacifier of the North. Cheng Tianzuo is an ordinary man who knows he is no ornament to the Song court. At Ruyang he took nine wounds and fell outside the hall; I pulled him out with my own hand.

sentences.zh: 凡人骨肉分張，並思集聚，輒已語之，但其弟苦辭。

translations.literal: When flesh and bone are scattered, ordinary people all wish to reunite — I have already told him so, but his younger brother firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When kin are torn apart, any man longs to be reunited — I have told him so, but his brother steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 今令與來使相見。」

translations.literal: Now I have ordered him to meet the incoming envoy."
translations.idiomatic: I have now arranged for him to meet your envoy.

sentences.zh: 程天福謂使人曰：「兄受命汝陽，不能死節，各在一國，何煩相見。」

translations.literal: Cheng Tianfu said to the envoy: "My elder brother received his commission at Ruyang yet could not die for duty — each serves a different state; why trouble with a meeting?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tianfu told the envoy, "My brother took his post at Ruyang and failed to die in its defense. We serve different realms — why should we meet?

sentences.zh: 燾又送氈各一領，鹽各九種，并胡豉：「凡此諸鹽，各有所宜。

translations.literal: Tao again sent one blanket each, nine kinds of salt each, and fermented bean paste, saying: "Of all these salts, each has its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: Tao also sent a blanket apiece, nine varieties of salt each, and fermented bean paste, saying, "Each of these salts has its proper use.

sentences.zh: 白鹽是魏主自所食。

translations.literal: White salt is what the Wei ruler eats himself.
translations.idiomatic: White salt is what the Wei ruler eats himself.

sentences.zh: 黑鹽治腹脹氣懣，細刮取六銖，以酒服之。

translations.literal: Black salt treats abdominal distension and pent-up qi — scrape off finely six zhu and take it with wine.
translations.idiomatic: Black salt treats bloating and inner distress; scrape off six zhu finely and take it with wine.

sentences.zh: 胡鹽治目痛。

translations.literal: Hu salt treats eye pain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu salt relieves eye pain.

sentences.zh: 柔鹽不食，治馬脊創。

translations.literal: Soft salt is not for eating — it treats wounds on a horse's back.
translations.idiomatic: Soft salt is not for eating; it treats sores on a horse's back.

sentences.zh: 赤鹽、駁鹽、臭鹽、馬齒鹽四種，並不中食。

translations.literal: Red salt, mottled salt, stinking salt, and horseshoe salt — four kinds, none fit for eating.
translations.idiomatic: Red salt, speckled salt, foul salt, and horseshoe salt — these four are not edible.

sentences.zh: 胡豉亦中啖。

translations.literal: The fermented bean paste is also fit to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The fermented bean paste is good to eat as well.

sentences.zh: 黃甘幸彼所豐，可更見分。」

translations.literal: Sweet oranges — fortunately you have them in abundance — may we have another share?"
translations.idiomatic: You are rich in sweet oranges — might we have another share?

sentences.zh: 又云：「魏主致意太尉、安北，何不遣人來至我間。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Wei ruler sends regards to the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North — why not send someone to my camp?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Wei ruler asks the Grand Marshal and the Pacifier of the North: why not send someone to visit our camp?

sentences.zh: 彼此之情，雖不可盡，要須見我小大，知我老少，觀我為人。

translations.literal: Each other's feelings, though they cannot be fully expressed, must at least let you see my stature, know whether I am young or old, and observe what manner of man I am.
translations.idiomatic: Our feelings cannot be fully conveyed in words, but you should at least see my stature, know whether I am young or old, and judge what sort of man I am.

sentences.zh: 若諸佐不可遣，亦可使僮幹來。」

translations.literal: If your high officers cannot be sent, you may send servants and clerks."
translations.idiomatic: If your chief advisers cannot come, send clerks or attendants.

sentences.zh: 暢又宣旨答曰：「魏主形狀才力，久為來往所見。

translations.literal: Chang again conveyed the reply: "The Wei ruler's form and strength have long been seen in the exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: Chang relayed the reply: "The Wei ruler's stature and prowess have long been known through our exchanges.

sentences.zh: 李尚書親自銜命，不患彼此不盡，故不復遺使信。」

translations.literal: Minister Li personally bears his commission — there is no fear that each side will not speak fully, so no further envoy is needed."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li carries the message in person — we need not fear anything will be left unsaid, so there is no need to send anyone else.

sentences.zh: 又云：「魏主恨向所送馬，殊不稱意。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Wei ruler resents the horses sent earlier — they were quite unsatisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Wei ruler was displeased with the horses you sent earlier.

sentences.zh: 安北若須大馬，當更送之，脫須蜀馬，亦有佳者。」

translations.literal: If the Pacifier of the North needs large horses, more will be sent; if you need Shu horses, fine ones are also available."
translations.idiomatic: If the Pacifier of the North wants larger horses, we can send more; if you prefer horses from Shu, we have good ones.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「安北不乏良駟，送自彼意，非此所求。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "The Pacifier of the North lacks no fine steeds — the gift came from your side's courtesy, not what we sought here."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The Pacifier of the North has no lack of fine horses — your gift was your own courtesy, not something we requested.

sentences.zh: 義恭餉燾炬燭十挺，世祖亦致錦一匹，曰：「知更須黃甘，誠非所吝。

translations.literal: Yigong presented Tao ten bundles of torches and candles; Emperor Xiaowu also sent one bolt of brocade, saying: "Knowing you again need sweet oranges — we truly do not begrudge them.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong sent Tao ten bundles of torches and candles; Emperor Xiaowu also sent a bolt of brocade, saying, "Knowing you want more sweet oranges — we do not begrudge them.

sentences.zh: 但送不足周彼一軍，向給魏主，未應便乏，故不復重付。」

translations.literal: But what we send is not enough to supply your whole army; what was given to the Wei ruler before should not already be exhausted, so we do not send again."
translations.idiomatic: But what we can send would not feed your whole army, and what we gave the Wei ruler earlier should not be gone already — so we will not send more.

sentences.zh: 燾復求甘蔗、安石榴，暢曰：「石榴出自鄴下，亦當非彼所乏。」

translations.literal: Tao again asked for sugarcane and pomegranates; Chang said: "Pomegranates come from below Ye — you should not lack them there either."
translations.idiomatic: Tao asked again for sugarcane and pomegranates. Chang said, "Pomegranates grow around Ye — you should not be short of them on your side.

sentences.zh: 孝伯又曰：「君南土膏粱，何為著屩。

translations.literal: Xiaobo again said: "You are a fine gentleman of the south — why wear straw sandals?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo added, "You are a refined man of the south — why wear straw sandals?

sentences.zh: 君而著此，使將士云何？」

translations.literal: If you wear these, what example for officers and soldiers?"
translations.idiomatic: If you dress like this, what are your officers and men to do?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「膏粱之言，誠為多愧。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Your words about a fine gentleman — truly much to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Your compliment is more than I deserve.

sentences.zh: 但以不武，受命統軍，戎陣之間，不容緩服。」

translations.literal: But because I am not martial, yet received command of the army — in the midst of battle there is no room for leisurely dress."
translations.idiomatic: But I am no warrior, and having been put in command, I cannot wear soft clothes in the face of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 孝伯又曰：「長史，我是中州人，久處北國，自隔華風，相去步武，不得致盡，邊皆是北人聽我語者，長史當深得我。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo again said: "Chief Secretary, I am a man of the Central Provinces, long resident in the northern state, naturally separated from refined custom — a few paces apart, we cannot speak fully; here on the border all who hear me are northerners — you, Chief Secretary, should understand me deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said again, "Chief Secretary, I am a man of the Central Plains who has lived long in the north and lost touch with civilized ways — a few steps apart, we cannot say all we mean. Everyone here who hears me is a northerner; you should understand me better than they do.

sentences.zh: 孝伯又曰：「永昌王，魏主從弟，自復常鎮長安，今領精騎八萬，直造淮南，壽春久閉門自固，不敢相禦。

translations.literal: Xiaobo again said: "Prince Yongchang, the Wei ruler's cousin, has long garrisoned Chang'an; now he leads eighty thousand elite cavalry straight toward Huainan — Shouchun has long closed its gates and holds fast, not daring to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Prince Yongchang, the Wei ruler's cousin, has long held Chang'an; he now leads eighty thousand elite horsemen straight for Huainan. Shouchun has shut its gates for ages and dares not meet him.

sentences.zh: 向送劉康祖頭，彼之所見。

translations.literal: Recently Liu Kangzu's head was sent — you on your side have seen it.
translations.idiomatic: We sent you Liu Kangzu's head — you have seen that.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨甚是所悉，亦是常才耳。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo is well known to us — merely ordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: We know Wang Xuemo well enough — he is nothing extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 南國何意作如此任使，以致奔敗。

translations.literal: Why did the southern state assign such people, leading to flight and defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Why did the south appoint such men and bring on rout and ruin?

sentences.zh: 自入此境七百餘里，主人竟不能一相拒逆。

translations.literal: Since entering this territory seven hundred-odd li, the host has not once been able to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Since we crossed your border seven hundred li, your side has not once stood in our way.

sentences.zh: 鄒山之險，君家所憑，前鋒始得接手，崔邪利便藏入穴，我間諸將倒曳腳而出之，魏主賜其生命，今從在此。

translations.literal: The peril of Zou Mountain, which your house relies on — our vanguard had barely engaged when Cui Xieli hid in a cave; our generals dragged him out by the feet; the Wei ruler spared his life and he now follows us here.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Mountain is your stronghold — yet when our vanguard barely engaged, Cui Xieli hid in a cave. Our generals hauled him out by the legs; the Wei ruler spared him, and he is here with us now.

sentences.zh: 復何以輕脫遣馬文恭至蕭縣，使望風退撓邪。

translations.literal: Again why lightly and casually send Ma Wengong to Xiao County, making him flee at sight of the wind?
translations.idiomatic: And why send Ma Wengong to Xiaoxian so rashly, only to have him break and run at the first alarm?

sentences.zh: 君家民人甚相忿怨，云清平之時，賦我租帛，至有急難，不能相拯。」

translations.literal: Your house's people are very resentful, saying: in peaceful times you taxed our grain and cloth — when crisis came, you could not save us."
translations.idiomatic: Your people are full of grievance, saying that in peaceful times you took their grain and cloth in taxes, but when trouble came you could not protect them.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「知永昌已過淮南，康祖為其所破，比有信使，無此消息。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Knowing Yongchang has already passed Huainan, Kangzu was defeated by him — recent envoys have brought no such news.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "We know Prince Yongchang has crossed into Huainan and that Kangzu was defeated — but our latest messengers brought no such report.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨南土偏將，不謂為才，但以人為前驅引導耳。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo is a minor southern general — not considered talented, merely sent as a guide in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo is a secondary southern commander — we never counted him a genius, only used him as a pathfinder.

sentences.zh: 大軍未至而河冰向合，玄謨量宜反旆，未為失機，但因夜回師，致戎馬小亂耳。

translations.literal: The main army had not arrived and the river ice was about to close — Xuemo judged it fit to turn back, not a lost opportunity, only because returning by night there was slight disorder among troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The main force had not yet arrived and the river was freezing — Xuemo judged it wise to withdraw, not a missed chance; only the night march caused a little confusion among the troops.

sentences.zh: 我家玄謨斗城，陳憲小將，魏主傾國，累旬不克。

translations.literal: Our Xuemo held a city the size of a dou; Chen Xian is a minor general — the Wei ruler threw the whole state at them and could not take them in many weeks.
translations.idiomatic: Our Xuemo held a city no bigger than a measure; Chen Xian is a minor commander — yet the Wei ruler threw the whole kingdom at them and could not win for weeks.

sentences.zh: 胡盛之偏裨小帥，眾無一旅，始濟融水，魏國君臣奔迸，僅得免脫，滑臺之師，無所多愧。

translations.literal: Hu Shengzhi, a minor subordinate commander, with forces not even one brigade — just crossing the Rong River, Wei ministers and ruler fled in panic, barely escaping — the force at Huatai, nothing much to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shengzhi was a petty officer with less than a brigade — yet when he crossed the Rong River, Wei ministers and ruler fled in panic and barely escaped. As for the army at Huatai, we have little to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 鄒山小戍，雖有微險，河畔之民，多是新附，始慕聖化，奸盜未息，亦使崔邪利撫之而已，今沒虜手，何損於國。

translations.literal: Zou Mountain's small garrison, though with slight peril — the riverside people are mostly newly submitted, just admiring sacred transformation, banditry not yet stilled — only had Cui Xieli pacify them; now fallen into barbarian hands — what loss to the state?
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Zou Mountain offered some slight defense, but the riverside folk are mostly new subjects still settling under our rule, with banditry not yet suppressed — Cui Xieli was there merely to keep order. If he has fallen into your hands, what harm is that to the state?

sentences.zh: 魏主自以十萬師而制一崔邪利，方復足言邪？

translations.literal: The Wei ruler himself with a hundred thousand troops subduing one Cui Xieli — is that even worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: Is it worth boasting that the Wei ruler needed a hundred thousand men to catch one Cui Xieli?

sentences.zh: 聞蕭、相百姓，並依山險，聊遣馬文恭以十隊示之耳。

translations.literal: Hearing the people of Xiao and Xiang all rely on mountain peril — only sent Ma Wengong with ten squads to show them.
translations.idiomatic: We heard the people of Xiao and Xiang had taken to the hills — we sent Ma Wengong with ten squads merely to show them our flag.

sentences.zh: 文恭謂前以三隊出，還走後，大營嵇玄敬以百騎至留城，魏軍奔敗。

translations.literal: Wengong says: previously three squads went out and returned in flight — afterward the main camp's Ji Xuanjing with a hundred riders reached Liucheng and the Wei army fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wengong says his three squads withdrew as planned — whereupon Ji Xuanjing of the main camp reached Liucheng with a hundred riders and routed your army.

sentences.zh: 輕敵致此，亦非所衄。

translations.literal: Light contempt of the enemy led to this — also not a real setback.
translations.idiomatic: A rash underestimation brought that about — hardly a defeat to speak of.

sentences.zh: 王境人民，列居河畔，二國交兵，當互加撫養，而魏師入境，肆行殘虐，事生意外，由彼無道。

translations.literal: People of the royal domain line the riverbanks — when two states cross arms, each should nurture the other; yet the Wei army entering the territory wantonly practices cruelty — matters arose unexpectedly through their lack of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Our people stand along the river — when two realms make war, each side should protect the other. Your army entered and ravaged at will; whatever uproar followed came from your own want of decency.

sentences.zh: 官不負民，民何怨人。

translations.literal: The officials do not fail the people — why should the people resent us?
translations.idiomatic: The court has not wronged the people — why should they hold grievances against us?

sentences.zh: 知入境土，百無相拒，此自上由太尉神算，次在鎮軍聖略。

translations.literal: Knowing entry into the territory, not once resisted — this above all is due to the Grand Marshal's divine calculation, next to the Field Marshal's sage strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Your army has marched seven hundred li without meeting resistance — that is first the Grand Marshal's master strategy, and second the Field Marshal's wise plans.

sentences.zh: 經國之要，雖不豫聞，然用兵有機，間亦不容相語。」

translations.literal: The essentials of governing the state — though not privy to them in advance — yet in employing troops there are opportune moments; occasionally one also cannot tell each other."
translations.idiomatic: I am not privy to every detail of statecraft, and the art of war has its secrets — some things cannot be shared even in talk like this.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「魏主當不圍此城，自率眾軍，直造瓜步。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The Wei ruler will likely not besiege this city — he himself will lead the armies straight to Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Wei ruler will probably not bother with this city — he will lead his host straight to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 南事若辦，彭城不待圍；

translations.literal: If the southern affair succeeds, Pengcheng need not wait for siege;
translations.idiomatic: If the southern campaign succeeds, Pengcheng will fall without a siege;

sentences.zh: 若不捷，彭城亦非所須也。

translations.literal: if not victorious, Pengcheng is also not needed.
translations.idiomatic: if it fails, Pengcheng will not matter anyway.

sentences.zh: 我今當南飲江湖，以療渴耳。」

translations.literal: I now shall go south to drink the rivers and lakes to cure thirst."
translations.idiomatic: I am going south to drink from the Yangtze — to slake my thirst.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「去留之事，自適彼懷。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Matters of going and staying — let them suit your own heart.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Whether you stay or go is entirely your affair.

sentences.zh: 若虜馬遂得飲江，便為無復天道。

translations.literal: If barbarian horses indeed get to drink from the river, then truly there is no Heaven's Way left.
translations.idiomatic: If your horses truly reach the Yangtze, Heaven itself will have forsaken us.

sentences.zh: 各應反命，遲復更悉。」

translations.literal: Each should return to report — later again more will be known."
translations.idiomatic: We each have our reports to deliver — we shall speak again in due time.

sentences.zh: 暢便回還，孝伯追曰：「長史深自愛敬，相去步武，恨不執手。」

translations.literal: Chang then turned back; Xiaobo called after him: "Chief Secretary, I deeply esteem and respect you — a few paces apart, regret we cannot clasp hands."
translations.idiomatic: Chang turned to go. Xiaobo called after him, "Chief Secretary, I think highly of you — we stand so close, yet I regret we cannot shake hands.

sentences.zh: 暢因復謂曰：「善將愛，冀蕩定有期，相見無遠。

translations.literal: Chang then again said: "Take good care — hope pacification will have its term, meeting not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Chang turned back once more and said, "Take care of yourself. May peace come soon, and may we meet again before long.

sentences.zh: 君若得還宋朝，今為相識之始。」

translations.literal: If you ever return to the Song court, today is the beginning of acquaintance."
translations.idiomatic: If you ever return to the Song court, let today be the day our friendship began.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「待此未期。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "To wait for that — not yet expected."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "That day is not one I expect to see.

sentences.zh: 燾又遣就二王借箜篌、琵琶、箏、笛等器及棊子，義恭答曰：「受任戎行，不齎樂具。

translations.literal: Tao again sent to the two princes to borrow konghou, pipa, zheng, flute and other instruments and go stones; Yigong answered: "Receiving command on campaign, did not bring musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent again to borrow konghou, pipa, zheng, flutes, and other instruments plus go stones. Yigong replied, "On campaign we brought no musical gear.

sentences.zh: 在此燕會，政使鎮府命妓，有弦百條，是江南之美，今以相致。」

translations.literal: Entertainments here at the banquet — merely had the commandery staff summon entertainers; there are a hundred stringed instruments, beauties of Jiangnan — now send them as gifts."
translations.idiomatic: For our feasts here we had the headquarters send entertainers — a hundred strings, the finest of Jiangnan — and offer them to you now.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「任居方岳，初不此經慮，且樂人常器，又觀前來諸王贈別，有此琵琶，今以相與。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu said: "Holding a regional post, at first did not anticipate this; besides, entertainers' usual instruments — also seeing former visiting princes' parting gifts, there is this pipa — now give it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu said, "In my border command I did not think to bring such things. These are our musicians' everyday instruments; noting what visiting princes gave in parting, I also have this pipa — take it.

sentences.zh: 棊子亦付。」

translations.literal: Go stones also delivered."
translations.idiomatic: The go stones are included as well.

sentences.zh: 孝伯言辭辯贍，亦北土之美也。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's words were eloquent and ample — a northern man's excellence as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's speech was fluent and rich — another fine specimen of the northern school.

sentences.zh: 暢隨宜應答，吐屬如流，音韻詳雅，風儀華潤，孝伯及左右人並相視歎息。

translations.literal: Chang answered as the occasion required; his utterances flowed like water, his tone refined and elegant, his bearing splendid and lustrous — Xiaobo and those beside him all looked at one another and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Chang matched him point for point, words pouring forth without pause, voice measured and graceful, presence radiant — Xiaobo and his attendants exchanged glances and murmured in wonder.

sentences.zh: 虜尋攻彭城南門，並放火，暢躬自前戰，身先士卒。

translations.literal: The barbarians soon attacked Pengcheng's south gate and set fires as well; Chang personally went forward to fight, taking the lead ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy soon assailed Pengcheng's south gate and torched the approaches. Chang fought in the front rank himself, leading the men from the van.

sentences.zh: 及燾自瓜步北走，經彭城下過，遣人語城內：「食盡且去，須麥熟更來。」

translations.literal: When Tao fled north from Guabu and passed below Pengcheng, he sent someone to tell those inside the city: "Provisions are exhausted and we depart for now; when the wheat ripens we shall return."
translations.idiomatic: When Tao withdrew north from Guabu and marched past Pengcheng, he sent word into the city: "Our grain is spent and we are leaving — but when the wheat is ripe, we shall be back.

sentences.zh: 義恭大懼，閉門不敢追。

translations.literal: Yigong was greatly afraid, shut the gates, and did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was terrified. He shut the gates and would not give chase.

sentences.zh: 虜期又至，議欲芟麥剪苗，移民堡聚，眾論並不同，復更會議。

translations.literal: When the barbarians' deadline drew near again, there was discussion of reaping the wheat, cutting the seedlings, and moving the people into fortified clusters; the assembled opinions all differed, and they met again to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy's promised return drew near, officials debated reaping the wheat, uprooting the young crops, and herding the populace into fortified settlements. Opinion was divided, and they convened again.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍錄事參軍王孝孫獨曰：「虜不能復來，既自可保，如其更至，此議亦不可立。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaosun, Recorder of the Pacification Army headquarters, alone said: "The barbarians cannot come again — in that case we can protect ourselves as we are; if they do return, this plan still cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaosun, staff recorder of the Pacification Army, spoke alone: "If the barbarians are not coming back, we can hold the city as we are. And if they do come, this plan still will not work.

sentences.zh: 百姓閉在內城，饑饉日久，方春之月，野采自資，一入堡聚，餓死立至。

translations.literal: The common people, shut inside the inner city, had long suffered famine; in the spring months they supported themselves by gathering in the wild — once forced into fortified clusters, death by starvation would come at once.
translations.idiomatic: The people, penned in the inner city, had been hungry for months. In early spring they survived by foraging in the fields — force them into stockades and they will starve at once.

sentences.zh: 民知必死，何可制邪？

translations.literal: When the people know they must die, how can they be controlled?
translations.idiomatic: Once people know they are being sent to their deaths, how can you restrain them?

sentences.zh: 虜若必來，芟麥無晚。」

translations.literal: If the barbarians truly come, reaping the wheat will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy truly comes, there will still be time to cut the wheat.

sentences.zh: 四坐默然，莫之敢對。

translations.literal: All present fell silent; none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: The hall went silent. No one dared answer.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「孝孫之議，實有可尋。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Xiaosun's proposal truly has points worth pursuing."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Xiaosun's argument has real merit.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍府典籤董元嗣侍世祖側，進曰：「王錄事議不可奪，實如來論。」

translations.literal: Dong Yuansi, chief clerk of the Pacification Army headquarters, attending at Emperor Xiaowu's side, stepped forward and said: "Recorder Wang's plan cannot be set aside — it is exactly as just argued."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuansi, headquarters chief clerk, standing at Emperor Xiaowu's side, stepped forward: "Recorder Wang's view cannot be overturned — it is precisely as stated.

sentences.zh: 別駕王子夏因曰：「此論誠然。」

translations.literal: Vice-Prefect Wang Zixia then said: "This argument is indeed so."
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Prefect Wang Zixia added, "That is certainly true.

sentences.zh: 暢斂板白世祖曰：「下官欲命孝孫彈子夏。」

translations.literal: Chang gathered his tablet and reported to Emperor Xiaowu: "Your humble servant wishes to have Xiaosun impeach Zixia."
translations.idiomatic: Chang straightened his tablet and addressed Emperor Xiaowu: "I wish to have Xiaosun bring charges against Zixia.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「王別駕有何事邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu said: "What matter has Vice-Prefect Wang?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu asked, "What has the vice-prefect done?

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「芟麥移民，可謂大議，一方安危，事繫於此。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Reaping wheat and moving the people — this may be called a great deliberation; the safety of the whole region hangs on it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Reaping the wheat and relocating the people is a matter of grave consequence — the region's fate depends on it.

sentences.zh: 子夏親為州端，曾無同異，及聞元嗣之言，則歡笑酬答，阿意左右，何以事君。」

translations.literal: Zixia personally stands at the head of the province, yet had no opinion of his own; once he heard Yuansi's words, he answered with laughter and assent, flattering those beside him — how is this to serve one's lord?"
translations.idiomatic: Zixia is the province's leading officer, yet he offered no view of his own; the moment Yuansi spoke, he laughed and agreed, currying favor with those around him. How does such a man serve his prince?

sentences.zh: 子夏大慚，元嗣亦有慚色。

translations.literal: Zixia was deeply ashamed; Yuansi too showed shame on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Zixia flushed with shame; Yuansi looked abashed as well.

sentences.zh: 義恭之議遂寢。

translations.literal: Yigong's proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞暢屢有正議，甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard that Chang repeatedly offered upright counsel and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard that Chang had spoken rightly again and again, and commended him warmly.

sentences.zh: 世祖猶停彭城，召暢先反，並使履行盱眙城，欲立大鎮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was still stationed at Pengcheng; he summoned Chang to return first and also had him inspect Xuyi city, intending to establish a major garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu remained at Pengcheng. He recalled Chang ahead of the main force and sent him to survey Xuyi, planning to make it a major stronghold.

sentences.zh: 時虜聲云當出襄陽，故以暢為南譙王義宣司空長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: At the time barbarian reports said they would move out from Xiangyang, so Chang was made Chief Secretary to the Minister of Works under the Prince of Nan Qiao, Yixuan, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then held that the enemy would strike from Xiangyang, so Chang was appointed Chief Secretary to Yixuan, Prince of Nan Qiao, in his capacity as Minister of Works, and made Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又欲暢代劉興祖為青州及彭城都督，竝不果。

translations.literal: They also wished Chang to replace Liu Xingzu as Commander of Qing Province and Pengcheng — neither appointment came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: There was also talk of appointing Chang in Liu Xingzu's place as regional commander of Qing and Pengcheng — none of it materialized.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元兇弑逆，義宣發哀之日，即便舉兵，暢為元佐，居僚首，哀容俯仰，廕映當時。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when the Depraved One murdered and usurped, on the day Yixuan proclaimed mourning he at once raised troops; Chang served as his chief aide, standing first among the staff — in the bearing of his mourning, rising and bowing, he cast a shade over the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, after the Depraved One's regicide, Yixuan took up arms the very day he declared mourning. Chang was his chief lieutenant and head of the staff; in every bow and gesture of grief he outshone all around him.

sentences.zh: 舉哀畢，改服，著黃韋絝褶，出射堂簡人，音姿容止，莫不矚目，見之者皆願為盡命。

translations.literal: When mourning was finished, he changed dress, put on yellow leather trousers and jacket, went out to the archery hall to select men — voice, bearing, and deportment; none failed to fix their eyes on him; those who saw him all wished to give their lives for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning rites ended, he changed clothes, donned yellow leather campaign dress, and went to the archery ground to review the troops. Voice, face, and bearing held every eye; men who saw him were ready to die in his service.

sentences.zh: 事平，徵為吏部尚書，夷道縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was summoned as Minister of Personnel, Marquis of Yidao County, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was recalled as Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidao, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 義宣既有異圖，蔡超等以暢民望，勸義宣留之，乃解南蠻校尉以授暢，加冠軍將軍，領丞相長史。

translations.literal: Once Yixuan already harbored divergent designs, Cai Chao and others, because of Chang's standing among the people, urged Yixuan to keep him; he therefore removed the post of Colonel of the Southern Man and granted it to Chang, promoted him to General Who Establishes Might, and had him serve as Chief Secretary to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan's treasonous intent became clear, Cai Chao and others, citing Chang's public prestige, urged Yixuan to retain him. Yixuan relinquished the post of Colonel of the Southern Man to Chang, promoted him to General Who Establishes Might, and made him Chief Secretary to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 暢遣門生荀僧寶下都，因顏竣陳義宣釁狀。

translations.literal: Chang sent his student Xun Sengbao down to the capital to report Yixuan's signs of rebellion through Yan Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chang dispatched his protégé Xun Sengbao to the capital to lay Yixuan's rebellious designs before Yan Jun.

sentences.zh: 僧寶有私貨停巴陵，不時下，會義宣起兵，津徑斷絕，僧寶遂不得去。

translations.literal: Sengbao had private goods detained at Baling and did not descend in time; just then Yixuan raised troops, ferry routes and roads were cut off, and Sengbao could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbao had private merchandise held up at Baling and did not reach the capital in time. Yixuan then rose in arms, the routes were severed, and Sengbao could not get away.

sentences.zh: 義宣將為逆，遣嬖人翟靈寶謂暢：「朝廷簡練舟甲，意在西討，今欲發兵自衛。」

translations.literal: As Yixuan was about to rebel, he sent his favorite Zhai Lingbao to tell Chang: "The court is drilling ships and armor, intending a western campaign; we now wish to mobilize troops for self-defense."
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of rebellion, Yixuan sent his favorite Zhai Lingbao to Chang: "The court is fitting out ships and armor for a campaign westward. We mean to raise troops in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「必無此理，請以死保之。」

translations.literal: Chang said: "Surely there is no such design — I ask to guarantee it with my life."
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "That cannot be true. I stake my life on it.

sentences.zh: 靈寶知暢不回，勸義宣殺以徇眾。

translations.literal: Lingbao, knowing Chang would not turn back, urged Yixuan to kill him to show the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Chang would not be moved, Lingbao urged Yixuan to execute him as an example to the troops.

sentences.zh: 即遣召暢，止於東齋，彌日不與相見，賴司馬竺超民保持，故獲全免。

translations.literal: He at once sent to summon Chang and detained him in the east study; for a whole day he would not meet him — thanks to Marshal Zhu Chaomin's protection, he was spared intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan summoned Chang and kept him in the east wing, refusing to see him all day. Only Marshal Zhu Chaomin's protection saved his life.

sentences.zh: 既而進號撫軍，別立軍部，以收民望。

translations.literal: Soon after he was advanced in title to Pacification General and a separate military staff was established, to gather popular esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Pacification General and given a separate military staff, all to win back public favor.

sentences.zh: 暢雖署文檄，而飲酒常醉，不省文書。

translations.literal: Though Chang signed proclamations and dispatches, he was constantly drunk on wine and did not attend to documents.
translations.idiomatic: Chang still put his name to manifestos, but he drank himself insensible and ignored the paperwork.

sentences.zh: 隨義宣東下，梁山戰敗，義宣奔走，暢於兵亂自歸，為軍人所掠，衣服都盡。

translations.literal: Following Yixuan eastward, they were defeated at Liangshan; Yixuan fled in panic; amid the military turmoil Chang surrendered on his own, was plundered by soldiers, and lost every stitch of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yixuan east. At Liangshan they were routed; Yixuan fled in disarray. In the chaos Chang gave himself up, was stripped by soldiers, and left with nothing to wear.

sentences.zh: 值右將軍王玄謨乘輿出營，暢已得敗衣，排玄謨上輿，玄謨意甚不悅，諸將欲殺之，隊主張世營救得免。

translations.literal: It happened that Right General Wang Xuanmo was riding in a carriage out of camp; Chang, having obtained cast-off clothes, pushed Xuanmo aside and mounted the carriage — Xuanmo was very displeased; the generals wished to kill him, but squad chief Zhang Shi rescued him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Right General Wang Xuanmo was leaving camp in his carriage. Chang, clad in rags he had scrounged, shoved Xuanmo aside and climbed aboard. Xuanmo was furious; the officers wanted him dead, but squad leader Zhang Shi intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 送京師，下廷尉，削爵土，配左右尚方。

translations.literal: He was sent to the capital, handed down to the Court of Justice, stripped of rank and fief, and assigned to the Left and Right Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the capital, tried by the Court of Justice, stripped of title and lands, and consigned to penal service in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 尋見原。

translations.literal: Before long he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon forgiven.

sentences.zh: 復起為都官尚書，轉侍中，代子淹領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was raised again as Minister of Justice, transferred to Palace Attendant, and replaced Zi Yan as Leader of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Minister of Justice, then made Palace Attendant and, in place of Zi Yan, Leader of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，出為會稽太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he went out as Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian he was posted as Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，卒官，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he died in office, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he died in office, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 顏竣表世祖：「張暢遂不救疾。

translations.literal: Yan Jun memorialized Emperor Xiaowu: "Zhang Chang finally could not be cured of his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun wrote to Emperor Xiaowu: "Zhang Chang's illness proved beyond cure.

sentences.zh: 東南之秀，蚤樹風範，聞問悽愴，深切常懷。」

translations.literal: A fine talent of the southeast, he early established a model of conduct — hearing the news, I am deeply grieved and carry it always in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: A leading light of the southeast, he set his example early. The news fills me with sorrow that will not leave me.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xuanzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Xuanzi.
