sentences.zh: 暢愛弟子輯，臨終遺命與輯合墳。

translations.literal: Chang loved his student Ji; on his deathbed he left instructions to share a tomb with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Chang doted on his protégé Ji and on his deathbed ordered that they be buried together.

sentences.zh: 暢弟悅，亦有美稱。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Yue also had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Yue was likewise well regarded.

sentences.zh: 歷中書吏部郎，侍中，臨海王子頊前軍長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: He passed through the posts of Secretariat Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Palace Attendant, Chief Secretary to the Vanguard Army under the Prince of Linhai, Zixiang, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Palace Attendant, Chief Secretary to the Vanguard Army under Prince Zixiang of Linhai, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛建偽號於尋陽，召為吏部尚書，與鄧琬共輔偽政。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, established a false reign at Xunyang, Yue was summoned as Minister of Personnel and together with Deng Wan supported the usurping government.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an proclaimed a rival throne at Xunyang, Yue was called to serve as Minister of Personnel and, with Deng Wan, upheld the pretender's regime.

sentences.zh: 事敗，殺琬歸降，事在《琬傳》。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, he killed Wan and returned in surrender — the matter is in the Biography of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, he killed Wan and submitted to the throne; the account is in Deng Wan's biography.

sentences.zh: 復為太子庶子，仍除巴陵王休若衛軍長史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: He was again made Crown Prince Household Companion, then appointed Chief Secretary to the Guard Army under the Prince of Baling, Xiuruo, and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as Crown Prince Household Companion, then made Chief Secretary to Prince Xiuruo of Baling's Guard Army and Administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，即代休若為雍州刺史、寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he immediately replaced Xiuruo as Inspector of Yong Province and General of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he succeeded Xiuruo as Inspector of Yong Province and General of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 復為休若征西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: He again served as Chief Secretary to the West-Pacifying Army under Xiuruo and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Chief Secretary to Xiuruo's West-Pacifying Army and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六年，太宗於巴郡置三巴校尉，以悅補之，加持節、輔師將軍，領巴郡太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Emperor Xiaowu established the Colonel of the Three Ba in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue to fill the post, adding the Staff of Authority and the title General Who Assists the Army, with concurrent service as Administrator of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Emperor Xiaowu created the post of Colonel of the Three Ba in Ba Commandery and appointed Yue to it, granting the Staff of Authority and the title General Who Assists the Army, with concurrent duty as Administrator of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the appointment, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 何偃，字仲弘，廬江灊人，司空尚之中子也。

translations.literal: He Yan, style Zhonghong, was a man of Qian in Lujiang — the middle son of Minister of Works Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, styled Zhonghong, was a native of Qian in Lujiang and the middle son of Minister of Works He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 州辟議曹從事，舉秀才，除中軍參軍，臨川王義慶平西府主簿。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Attendant in the Deliberation Bureau; he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt candidate, appointed Army Adjutant of the Central Army, and Master of Records in the West-Pacifying headquarters of the Prince of Linchuan, Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: The province engaged him as a deliberation clerk; he was nominated as a Filial and Incorrupt candidate, made Army Adjutant of the Central Army, and Master of Records on the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing's West-Pacifying staff.

sentences.zh: 召為太子洗馬，不拜。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Crown Prince Groom, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to serve as Crown Prince Groom but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十九年，為丹陽丞，除廬陵王友，太子中舍人，中書郎，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he served as Assistant Administrator of Danyang, then was appointed Companion to the Prince of Luling, Crown Prince Household Middle Attendant, Secretariat Gentleman, and Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yuanjia he became Assistant Administrator of Danyang, then Companion to the Prince of Luling, Crown Prince Household Middle Attendant, Secretariat Gentleman, and Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 時義陽王昶任東官，使偃行義陽國事。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Yiyang, Chang, held office in the Eastern Palace, and Yan was made to administer the affairs of the Yiyang fief.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Chang of Yiyang served in the Eastern Palace, and Yan was entrusted with the administration of the Yiyang fief.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，太祖欲更北伐，訪之群臣，偃議曰：「內幹胡法宗宣詔，逮問北伐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when Emperor Wen wished to launch another northern campaign, he consulted the ministers; Yan argued: "The Internal Attendant Hu Fazong proclaimed the edict and immediately asked about the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, as Emperor Wen prepared another northern campaign, he sought his ministers' counsel. Yan argued: "When Internal Attendant Hu Fazong read the edict, he pressed us at once on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 伏計賊審有殘禍，犬羊易亂，殲殄非難，誠如天旨。

translations.literal: I submit that the enemy truly suffers lingering ruin; dogs and sheep are easily thrown into disorder — to annihilate them is not difficult; this is indeed as Heaven intends.
translations.idiomatic: It is true, as Your Majesty holds, that the foe is already half-ruined — a herd easily scattered — and that crushing them should not be hard.

sentences.zh: 今雖廟算無遺，而士未精習。

translations.literal: Yet though the plans in the temple are without omission, the troops are not yet finely trained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though the court's plans leave nothing out, the troops are not yet well drilled.

sentences.zh: 緣邊鎮戍，充實者寡，邊民流散，多未附業。

translations.literal: Along the border, garrison towns that are fully manned are few; frontier people are scattered in flight, and many have not yet returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Border garrisons are mostly understrength; frontier folk remain displaced, and many have not resumed their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 控引所資，取給根本。

translations.literal: What we rely on for control and supply is drawn from the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The resources on which any campaign must draw come from the heartland.

sentences.zh: 虧根本以殉邊患，宜動必萬克。

translations.literal: To impair the foundation while chasing border troubles — every move ought to be sure of ten-thousandfold success.
translations.idiomatic: If we weaken the heartland to answer a frontier crisis, every move must be certain of total victory.

sentences.zh: 無慮往歲挫傷，續以內釁，侮亡取亂，誠為沛然。

translations.literal: There is no doubt about last year's setbacks, followed by internal strife — to insult the dying and seize disorder is truly abundant in opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: No one doubts that last year's defeats and their ensuing internal troubles give us ample occasion to strike a weakened foe.

sentences.zh: 然淮、泗數州，實亦雕耗，流傭未歸，創痍未起。

translations.literal: Yet the several prefectures of Huai and Si are in truth also depleted; wandering laborers have not returned, and wounds have not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Huai and Si region itself is exhausted: refugees have not come home, and its wounds are still fresh.

sentences.zh: 且攻守不等，客主形異，薄之則勢艱，圍之則曠日，進退之間，奸虞互起。

translations.literal: Moreover attack and defense are not equal, guest and host differ in form — press closely and the situation grows hard; besiege and days stretch long; between advance and retreat, treachery and misgiving arise together.
translations.idiomatic: Attack and defense are not the same contest, nor are invader and defender matched in strength. Press too hard and the odds turn against us; lay siege and time runs out; in every advance or retreat, betrayal and doubt will multiply.

sentences.zh: 竊謂當今之弊易衄，方來之寇不深，宜含垢藏疾，以齊天道。」

translations.literal: I privately believe that today's weakness is prone to defeat, while the coming enemy threat is not deep — one ought to bear humiliation and conceal wounds, to align with Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: I believe our present weakness makes us easy to break, while the enemy's coming blow is not yet mortal. We should swallow our shame, nurse our injuries, and wait until we move with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 遷始興王濬征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Secretary to the North-Pacifying Army under the Prince of Shixing, Jun, and Administrator of South Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Secretary to Prince Jun of Shixing's North-Pacifying Army and made Administrator of South Donghai.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，以偃為侍中，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When the Depraved One murdered and established himself, Yan was made Palace Attendant, in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: After the Depraved One's regicide and usurpation, Yan was appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 時尚之為司空、尚書令，偃居門下，父子並處權要，時為寒心；

translations.literal: At the time Shangzhi was Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Yan served at the gate of the palace — father and son both held power — and the age shuddered for them;
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi was then Minister of Works and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, while Yan served at court — father and son together at the seat of power — and many feared for the realm;

sentences.zh: 而尚之及偃善攝機宜，曲得時譽。

translations.literal: yet Shangzhi and Yan were skilled at seizing the right moment, and by subtle means won the reputation of the age.
translations.idiomatic: yet Shangzhi and Yan handled affairs with tact and, by measured steps, kept public esteem.

sentences.zh: 會世祖即位，任遇無改，除大司馬長史，遷侍中，領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, their appointments and favor were unchanged; Yan was made Chief Secretary to the Grand Marshal, transferred to Palace Attendant, and given concurrent duty as Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, their standing did not change. Yan was made Chief Secretary to the Grand Marshal, then Palace Attendant and concurrent Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 時責百官讜言，偃以為：「宜重農恤本，並官省事，考課以知能否，增俸以除吏奸。

translations.literal: At the time the court demanded candid speech from all officials; Yan held that one should "stress agriculture and care for the foundation, consolidate offices and reduce affairs, examine performance to know ability, and raise salaries to remove official corruption.
translations.idiomatic: When the court called on every official for frank counsel, Yan argued that the state should "put agriculture first and tend the roots of the realm, merge redundant offices and lighten the burden of administration, test performance to separate the capable from the useless, and raise salaries to curb official corruption.

sentences.zh: 責成良守，久於其職。

translations.literal: Hold good prefects accountable and keep them long in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Hold good magistrates to their duties and leave them in office long enough to govern.

sentences.zh: 都督刺史，宜別其任。」

translations.literal: Area Commanders and Inspectors ought to have their duties separated."
translations.idiomatic: Separate the roles of area commander and provincial inspector."

sentences.zh: 改領驍騎將軍，親遇隆密，有加舊臣。

translations.literal: He was changed to concurrent service as General of Valiant Cavalry; imperial favor was lofty and close, exceeding that shown old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was given concurrent rank as General of Valiant Cavalry and enjoyed imperial favor deeper than that accorded even veteran ministers.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚之去選未五載，偃復襲其跡，世以為榮。

translations.literal: Shangzhi had left the selection office less than five years before; Yan again followed in his footsteps — the age took it for glory.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi had left the Ministry of Personnel fewer than five years earlier; when Yan succeeded to the same post, the court counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 侍中顏竣至是始貴，與偃俱在門下，以文義賞會，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yan Jun had only now risen to prominence; with Yan they were both at the palace gate, meeting in literary discussion and mutual appreciation — they got on very well.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yan Jun had only lately come into power. He and Yan served together at court, meeting over texts and ideas, and they were on excellent terms.

sentences.zh: 竣自謂任遇隆密，宜居重大，而位次與偃等未殊，意稍不悅。

translations.literal: Jun considered his appointment and favor lofty and close, and that he ought to hold weightier rank; yet his standing was not distinguished from Yan's — his mood grew somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jun believed his favor with the throne entitled him to greater standing, yet his rank was no higher than Yan's, and he grew quietly resentful.

sentences.zh: 及偃代竣領選，竣愈憤懣，與偃遂有隙。

translations.literal: When Yan replaced Jun in charge of selection, Jun grew all the more bitter; he and Yan then had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan succeeded Jun as head of personnel appointments, Jun's resentment deepened, and a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 竣時勢傾朝野，偃不自安，遂發心悸病，意慮乖僻，上表解職，告醫不仕。

translations.literal: Jun's power then tilted the court and countryside; Yan did not feel secure, and so developed palpitations; his thoughts turned contrary and strange; he submitted a memorial resigning office and pleaded illness to the physicians, refusing to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's influence then dominated court and country. Yan, ill at ease, developed a racing heart and a troubled mind. He memorialized to resign and pleaded illness, refusing office.

sentences.zh: 世祖遇偃既深，備加治療，名醫上藥，隨所宜須，乃得瘥。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's regard for Yan was already deep; he fully provided treatment — famous physicians and superior medicines, whatever was needed — and only then was he cured.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, who favored Yan deeply, saw that he received every care — the best physicians and medicines, whatever he required — until he recovered.

sentences.zh: 時上長女山陰公主愛傾一時，配偃子戢。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's eldest daughter, the Princess of Shanyin, was beloved beyond all others of the age; she was matched to Yan's son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's eldest daughter, the Princess of Shanyin, was then the most favored woman at court; she was betrothed to Yan's son Ji.

sentences.zh: 素好談玄，注《莊子•消搖篇》傳於世。

translations.literal: He had long loved discussing the arcane and annotated the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of the Zhuangzi, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had always loved metaphysical discourse and wrote a commentary on the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of the Zhuangzi that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，卒官，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he died in office, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he died in office, at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 世祖與顏竣詔曰：「何偃遂成異世，美志長往。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict to Yan Jun: "He Yan has passed into another world; his fine aspirations have gone far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu wrote to Yan Jun: "He Yan has left this world, his noble aims gone with him.

sentences.zh: 與之周旋，重以姻媾，臨哭傷怨，良不能已。

translations.literal: In moving with him, bound moreover by marriage ties — facing his death I grieve and lament, truly unable to stop.
translations.idiomatic: I moved in his company for years, and we were joined by marriage besides. At his passing my grief is more than I can bear.

sentences.zh: 往矣如何！

translations.literal: He is gone — what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: He is gone — what is there to say!

sentences.zh: 宜贈散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，本官如故。」

translations.literal: He should be posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon; his original offices remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with his former offices recorded unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靖子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 子戢，升明末，為相國左長史。

translations.literal: His son Ji, at the end of the Shengming era, served as Left Chief Secretary to the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, at the end of the Shengming era, served as Left Chief Secretary to the Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 江智淵，濟陽考城人，湘州刺史夷弟子。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhiyuan was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang — a nephew of Yi, Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhiyuan was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang and a nephew of Jiang Yi, Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 父僧安，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: His father Seng'an was Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Seng'an had served as Crown Prince Household Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 智淵初為著作郎，江夏王義恭太尉行參軍，太子太傅主簿，隨王誕後軍參軍。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan first served as Editorial Director, Acting Army Adjutant to the Grand Marshal under the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, Master of Records to the Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, and Rear-Army Adjutant under the Prince of Sui, Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan began as Editorial Director, then served as Acting Army Adjutant on Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's Grand Marshal staff, Master of Records to the Crown Prince's Grand Tutor, and Rear-Army Adjutant under Prince Dan of Sui.

sentences.zh: 世父夷有盛名，夷子湛又有清譽，父子竝貴達，智淵父少無名問，湛禮敬甚簡，智淵常以為恨，自非節歲，不入湛門。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Yi had great fame; Yi's son Zhan also had a pure reputation — father and son were both honored and eminent; Zhiyuan's father had little renown; Zhan's courtesy was very perfunctory — Zhiyuan often took this as a grievance, and except on festival days would not enter Zhan's gate.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Jiang Yi enjoyed great renown, and Yi's son Jiang Zhan a spotless reputation — father and son both rose high. Zhiyuan's own father had won little fame, and Zhan's courtesy toward the branch was cold. Zhiyuan resented this deeply and, save on feast days, would not cross Zhan's threshold.

sentences.zh: 及為隨王誕佐，在襄陽，誕待之甚厚。

translations.literal: When he became an aide to Prince Dan of Sui, in Xiangyang, Dan treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as an aide to Prince Dan of Sui at Xiangyang, Dan treated him with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 時諮議參軍謝莊、府主簿沈懷文並與智淵友善。

translations.literal: At that time Advisory Staff Officer Xie Zhuang and Headquarters Master of Records Shen Huaiwen were both on friendly terms with Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Advisory Staff Officer Xie Zhuang and headquarters recorder Shen Huaiwen were both close friends of Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 懷文每稱之曰：「人所應有盡有，人所應無盡無者，其江智淵乎！」

translations.literal: Huaiwen often praised him, saying: "Whatever a man ought to have, he has in full; whatever a man ought not to have, he lacks entirely — is that not Jiang Zhiyuan!"
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen often said of him, "Whatever a man should possess, he has; whatever a man should lack, he lacks — who else could that be but Jiang Zhiyuan!"

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，除尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia he was appointed Secretariat Officer of the Storehouse Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanjia era he was appointed director in the Secretariat's storehouse bureau.

sentences.zh: 時高流官序，不為臺郎，智淵門孤援寡，獨有此選，意甚不說，固辭不肯拜。

translations.literal: At that time men of high standing in official rank did not serve as Secretariat gentlemen; Zhiyuan's house was isolated with few backers — he alone had this selection, and was very displeased, firmly declining and refusing to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Men of eminent standing at the time did not take Secretariat gentleman posts; Zhiyuan's family was isolated and poorly connected, and this lone appointment displeased him so deeply that he firmly refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕復版為驃騎參軍，轉主簿，隨府轉司空主簿、記室參軍，領南濮陽太守，遷從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince Dan of Jingling again summoned him as Rapid-Cavalry Army Adjutant, then Master of Records; following the prince's staff he became Master of Records to the Minister of Works, Army Staff Recorder, concurrent Administrator of Southern Puyang, and was promoted to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling recalled him as adjutant to the Rapid-Cavalry command, then chief clerk; he followed the prince's staff as chief clerk to the Ministry of Works and army staff recorder, served concurrently as governor of southern Puyang, and was promoted to staff attendant.

sentences.zh: 誕將為逆，智淵悟其機，請假先反。

translations.literal: When Dan was about to rebel, Zhiyuan perceived the signs and requested leave to return ahead of him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan was plotting rebellion, Zhiyuan sensed it and asked leave to return to the capital first.

sentences.zh: 誕事發，即除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Dan's affair broke out, he was at once appointed Secretariat Vice-Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan's plot was exposed, Zhiyuan was immediately appointed vice-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 智淵愛好文雅，詞采清贍，世祖深相知待，恩禮冠朝。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan loved refinement and elegance; his literary style was clear and ample; Emperor Xiaowu knew and treated him deeply, his favor and courtesy ranking first in court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan loved refined learning and wrote in a lucid, ample style; Emperor Xiaowu knew him well and favored him above all others at court.

sentences.zh: 上燕私甚數，多命群臣五三人游集，智淵常為其首。

translations.literal: The emperor's private banquets were very frequent; he often ordered three or five ministers to gather for outings, and Zhiyuan was regularly their chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held private banquets often and would summon three or five ministers at a time for outings — Zhiyuan was usually foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 同侶未及前，輒獨蒙引進，智淵每以越眾為慚，未嘗有喜色。

translations.literal: Before his companions could advance, he alone would be granted private audience; Zhiyuan was always ashamed at outstripping the rest and never showed a pleased expression.
translations.idiomatic: Before his companions could approach, he alone would be summoned in — Zhiyuan was always ashamed to outshine the others and never looked pleased by it.

sentences.zh: 每從遊幸，與群僚相隨，見傳詔馳來，知當呼己，聳動愧恧，形於容貌，論者以此多之。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed on tours of pleasure with the assembled officials, seeing an edict-bearer gallop up and knowing he would be summoned, he would start and flush with shame, showing it in his face — commentators for this held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial outings he walked among the officials; when he saw a courier gallop up with an edict and knew he would be called, he would start and flush with embarrassment — something critics admired in him.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry and Ministerial Recorder in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 上每酣宴，輒詬辱群臣，並使自相嘲訐，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor grew drunk at banquet, he would revile and humiliate the ministers and make them mock one another for his amusement.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor drank deeply at banquets, he would insult the ministers and set them to mocking one another for sport.

sentences.zh: 智淵素方退，漸不會旨。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was by nature upright and retiring, and gradually failed to suit the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan was upright and reserved by nature, and gradually fell out of step with the emperor's mood.

sentences.zh: 嘗使以王僧朗嘲戲其子景文，智淵正色曰：「恐不宜有此戲。」

translations.literal: Once the emperor had Wang Senglang mock his son Jingwen in sport; Zhiyuan with a stern face said: "I fear such sport is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had Wang Senglang jest at his son Jingwen; Zhiyuan said gravely, "I fear such jesting is not appropriate."

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「江僧安癡人，癡人自相惜。」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Jiang Seng'an was a fool — fools pity one another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "Jiang Seng'an was a fool — and fools stick up for each other."

sentences.zh: 智淵伏席流涕，由此恩寵大衰，出為新安王子鸞北中郎長史、南東海太守，加拜寧朔將軍，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan prostrated himself on the mat and wept; from this his favor greatly declined; he went out as Chief Secretary to Prince Luan of Xin'an's Northern Center Command, Administrator of South Donghai, with additional appointment as Pacifying-the-North General, acting for South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan bowed low at his place and wept. From then on imperial favor fell away sharply; he was posted out as chief secretary to Prince Luan of Xin'an's northern command and governor of South Donghai, with the additional rank of Pacifying-the-North General and charge of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，上寵姬宣貴妃殷氏卒，使群臣議諡，智淵上議曰「懷」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor's beloved consort Lady Yin of the Honored Consort of Xuan died, he had the ministers deliberate on her posthumous title; Zhiyuan submitted the proposal "Cherishing."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor's favorite, Honored Consort Yin of the Xuan rank, died, the court was asked to propose a posthumous title; Zhiyuan submitted "Cherishing."

sentences.zh: 上以不盡嘉號，甚銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because it was not a fully laudatory title, harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor felt the title was insufficiently flattering and bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 後車駕幸南山，乘馬至殷氏墓，群臣皆騎從，上以馬鞭指墓石柱謂智淵曰：「此上不容有懷字！」

translations.literal: Later the imperial carriage visited South Mountain; riding on horseback to Lady Yin's tomb, the ministers all followed on horseback; the emperor with his riding crop pointed at the tomb's stone pillar and said to Zhiyuan: "On this there may not be the character 'cherish'!"
translations.idiomatic: Later, on an outing to South Mountain, the emperor rode to Lady Yin's tomb with the ministers following on horseback; he pointed his riding crop at the stone pillar on the grave and told Zhiyuan, "That character 'cherish' must not appear here!"

sentences.zh: 智淵益惶懼。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan grew still more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan grew only more fearful.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，以憂卒，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming he died of grief, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming (463) he died of anxiety and grief at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 子季筠，太子洗馬，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Jijun was Crown Prince Groom of the Stable and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jijun served as groom of the stable to the crown prince and died young.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，以後父，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Later Deposed Emperor took the throne, as father of the empress he was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Houfei ascended the throne, Jijun was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon as the empress's father.

sentences.zh: 季筠妻王，平望鄉君。

translations.literal: Jijun's wife Wang was Lady of Pingwang Village.
translations.idiomatic: Jijun's wife, née Wang, held the title Lady of Pingwang.

sentences.zh: 智淵兄子概，早孤，養之如子。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's elder brother's son Kai, orphaned early, he raised as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's nephew Kai was orphaned young; Zhiyuan raised him as his own son.

sentences.zh: 概歷黃門吏部郎，侍中，武陵王北中郎長史、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: Kai passed through Yellow Gate and Ministerial Recorder posts, Palace Attendant, Chief Secretary to the Prince of Wuling's Northern Center Command, Administrator of South Donghai, acting for South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kai served as palace attendant and director in the Ministry of Personnel, then as chief secretary to the Prince of Wuling's northern command and governor of South Donghai, with charge of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era under the Later Deposed Emperor, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yuanhui era under Emperor Houfei.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫將帥者，御眾之名；

translations.literal: The historian says: A commander is the name for one who governs the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: The term "commander" denotes one who governs troops;

sentences.zh: 士卒者，一夫之用。

translations.literal: soldiers are the use of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers are the instrument of a single man.

sentences.zh: 坐談兵機，制勝千里，安在乎蒙楯前驅，履腸涉血而已哉！

translations.literal: To sit and discuss military stratagem, to overcome a thousand li away — how does that depend on bearing a shield and driving ahead, treading entrails and wading through blood alone!
translations.idiomatic: To sit and discuss strategy and prevail a thousand li away — what need is there merely to bear a shield in the van and tread through blood and entrails!

sentences.zh: 山濤之稱羊祜曰：「大將雖不須筋力，軍中猶宜強健。」

translations.literal: Shan Tao's praise of Yang Hu said: "A great general may not need physical strength, yet in the army one should still be robust."
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao said of Yang Hu, "A great general need not rely on brute strength, yet in the army robust health is still desirable."

sentences.zh: 以此為言，則叔子之幹力弱矣。

translations.literal: By this saying, then Shuzi's physical strength was weak.
translations.idiomatic: By that standard, Shuzi's physical vigor was slight.

sentences.zh: 杜預文士儒生，身不能穿札，射未嘗跨馬，一朝統大眾二十餘萬，為平吳都督。

translations.literal: Du Yu was a literary scholar and Confucian student — his body could not pierce a target; in archery he had never straddled a horse — yet in a morning he commanded a great host of more than two hundred thousand as Director-General for the Pacification of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu was a literati and Confucian scholar who could not pierce a target with an arrow and had never mounted a horse for archery — yet one morning he took command of more than two hundred thousand men as director-general for the conquest of Wu.

sentences.zh: 王戎把臂入林，亦受專征之寄。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, arm in arm entering the grove, also received the entrustment of independent campaign command.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, the man who linked arms with Ruan Ji in the bamboo grove, likewise received an independent military command.

sentences.zh: 何必山西猛士，六郡良家，然後可受脤於朝堂，荷推轂之重。

translations.literal: Why must there be fierce warriors of Shanxi and good families of the six commanderies before one may receive sacrificial flesh in the court hall and bear the weight of the chariot-push?
translations.idiomatic: Why must one be a fierce warrior of Shanxi or a son of a good family from the six commanderies before receiving investiture at court and bearing the weight of supreme command?

sentences.zh: 及虜兵深入，徐服恇震，非張暢正言，則彭、汴危矣。

translations.literal: When the barbarian armies penetrated deep, Xu and the coastal regions were shaken with fear — had it not been for Zhang Chang's upright words, Peng and Bian would have been in peril.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian armies drove deep inland and Xu Province trembled with fear, had it not been for Zhang Chang's forthright counsel, Pengcheng and Bian would have been lost.

sentences.zh: 豈其身捍飛鏑，手折雲衝，方足使窮揲假命，危城載安乎？

translations.literal: Was it only by his body blocking flying bolts and his hands breaking cloud-chariots that he could make the desperate divination gain life and the perilous city bear peace?
translations.idiomatic: Was it only by catching flying bolts with his body or snapping siege engines with his hands that he saved a doomed city and a desperate garrison?

sentences.zh: 仁者之有勇，非為臆說。

translations.literal: That the benevolent also have courage is no fanciful doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: That the benevolent can also be brave is no idle speculation.
